cases.title: Initiate drag event and capture product title and price
cases.description: Drag a product item (data-testid='product-item-1') from the product list and verify that the drag event successfully captures the product's title ('product-title-1') and price ('product-price-1') for transfer.

cases.title: Verify non-draggable elements do not initiate drag events
cases.description: Attempt to initiate a drag event on an element without the 'draggable=true' attribute and verify that the system does not capture any product title or price for transfer.

cases.title: Drop product item into drop area to update cart display
cases.description: Drag a product item (data-testid='product-item-1') and drop it into the designated drop area (id='div1', data-testid='drop-area'). Verify that the cart display automatically updates with the product title appearing in .box2, the unit price in .box3, and the quantity in .box1.

cases.title: Drop repeated products into drop area to increment quantity
cases.description: Drag and drop the same product item (data-testid='product-item-1') multiple times into the drop area (id='div1', data-testid='drop-area'). Verify that the system supports repeated products and increments the quantity accordingly in .box1.

cases.title: Calculate and display total price for multiple cart items
cases.description: Verify that the system correctly sums the prices of all products in the cart, formats the total to two decimal places with the currency symbol, and displays it in the div with id='allMoney'.

cases.title: Calculate and display total price for a single cart item
cases.description: Verify that the system correctly calculates and displays the total price formatted to two decimal places with the currency symbol in id='allMoney' when only a single product is present in the cart.

opinions.feedback: The proposed test cases are generally well-structured and cover the core requirements of dragging, dropping, cart updates, and total calculation. However, case G-002 tests a negative scenario ('non-draggable elements') that is not specified in requirement e2edev_bench_01-R-1, making it an unsupported edge case. Furthermore, cases G-005 and G-006 can be combined into a single robust test case covering both single and multiple cart items.
confirmed_blockers: Case G-002 tests non-draggable elements which is not mentioned in requirement e2edev_bench_01-R-1.

analysis.analysis: For requirement e2edev_bench_01-R-1: Normal scenario includes dragging a product item (e.g., product-item-1) and successfully capturing the product title (product-title-1) and price (product-price-1) via the drag event transfer. Edge or boundary scenarios include dragging an item without fully formed attributes or checking that non-draggable elements cannot initiate the drag. For requirement e2edev_bench_01-R-3: Normal scenario involves dropping product items (product-item-1, product-item-2) into the drop area (id='div1', data-testid='drop-area'), updating the cart display with product title in .box2, unit price in .box3, and quantity in .box1. Edge and abnormal scenarios include dropping repeated products to ensure quantity increments properly, and dropping invalid elements that are not part of the product list. For requirement e2edev_bench_01-R-5: Normal scenario includes calculating the total price of all items in the cart, formatting it to two decimal places with the currency symbol (e.g., '$80.00'), and displaying it in <div id='allMoney'>. Edge scenarios involve calculating the total with a single item, multiple items, or empty cart totals.

Verify that the cart display updates correctly for each item, showing their respective product titles in .box2, unit prices in .box3, and quantities in .box1.

cases.title: Calculate and display total price for cart items
cases.description: Verify that the system correctly sums the prices of all products in the cart (supporting both single and multiple items), formats the total to two decimal places with the appropriate currency symbol, and displays it in the div with id='allMoney'.

output.feedback: All proposed high-level test cases are clear, distinct, cover the requirements thoroughly, and are fully testable without any blockers.
All cases accurately map to their respective requirements and are fully actionable and testable.

output.analysis: For requirement e2edev_bench_01-R-1: Normal scenario includes dragging a product item (e.g., product-item-1) and successfully capturing the product title (product-title-1) and price (product-price-1) via the drag event transfer. Edge scenario involves verifying data transfer integrity for items with special characters or long text. For requirement e2edev_bench_01-R-3: Normal scenarios include dropping a single product item into the designated drop area (id='div1', data-testid='drop-area') and dropping multiple different product items (e.g., product-item-1 and product-item-2) into the drop area, verifying their respective displays in .box2 (title), .box3 (unit price), and .box1 (quantity). Edge and abnormal scenarios include dropping repeated products to ensure quantity increments properly, and dropping invalid elements not part of the product list. For requirement e2edev_bench_01-R-5: Normal scenario includes calculating the total price of all items in the cart, formatting it to two decimal places with the currency symbol (e.g., '$80.00'), and displaying it in <div id='allMoney'>. Edge scenarios cover both single and multiple mixed cart items summing up correctly.
